sections.heading: Date Picker
paragraphs: A single component set covering single-date, date-range, and date+time selection, with the calendar panel handled as a boolean property.

sections.heading: Anatomy — real Range example
paragraphs: ① Date field(s) — every field carries a trailing calendar icon, never leading. A range field renders two side by side sharing one popover.
② Presets — Today, Yesterday, Last 7/30 days, This/Last month; a side list next to the calendar.
③ Calendar — month grid(s); day-cell states (Default/Selected/In-range/Today) are baked as plain layers, never promoted to their own component.
④ Footer actions — Clear / Cancel / Apply, so a stray click never commits a half-made range selection.

sections.heading: Variants & States
paragraphs: Built as exactly 21 variants: Type(Single/Range/DateTime) × State(Default/Hover/Focused/Filled/Disabled/Read-only/Error) — an exact match to the component skill's own spec.

sections.heading: Token Map
paragraphs: component/date-picker collection: color/field/border/{default|hover|focused|disabled|read-only|error}, color/field/text/error, color/field/icon/error, color/calendar/border, and equivalents for the calendar day-cell reference states.

sections.heading: Behaviour & Accessibility
paragraphs: Month grid always renders 42 cells (6 full weeks) so grid height never jumps between months. Range selection: first click sets start, second sets end, a third click starts a new range; clicking before the current start moves the start instead of erroring. Arrow keys move focus day-to-day (left/right ±1, up/down ±7); Enter/Space selects; Escape closes without committing. Each day announces weekday, full date, and active state to assistive tech.

No gaps identified — this is one of the cleanest matches between skill and build reviewed across the file, including the subtle "don't componentize calendar internals" rule being followed precisely (day cells, presets, and month headers are all plain layers, never their own component). No Do's/Don'ts section: no consumer-facing rule in the source material had a genuine visual counterexample that wouldn't just restate the anatomy already shown above.
